skill.description: Guides agile sprint planning, backlog prioritization, capacity planning, velocity review, and sprint reporting with structured templates and practical planning frameworks.

security_audit.summary: The static alerts are false positives from Markdown backticks, fenced examples, planning formulas, and ordinary sprint board language. No evidence found of prompt injection, data exfiltration, hidden code execution, malware intent, or reconnaissance behavior in SKILL.md or templates/sprint-plan-template.md.

remediation.issue: Markdown command examples can look executable to automated scanners.
remediation.suggestion: Label commands as optional, user-approved examples and keep them limited to the stated sprint planning workflow.

remediation.issue: The skill references helper scripts that are not included in the reviewed package.
remediation.suggestion: Either include the scripts for review or remove script invocation examples from the skill instructions.

content.user_title: Plan Agile Sprints With Structured Guidance
content.value_statement: Sprint planning often lacks a clear link between goals, capacity, and backlog priority. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code create structured sprint plans, prioritize work, and track delivery risk.
actual_capabilities: Analyzes backlog items and helps select sprint scope.
Applies RICE, MoSCoW, WSJF, and value effort prioritization.
Calculates capacity using team size, sprint length, and availability.
Creates sprint goals, success criteria, and sprint plan sections.
Reviews burndown, velocity, blockers, and scope changes.
Supports sprint review and retrospective planning.
limitations: Requires accurate backlog, velocity, and capacity data from the user or connected tools.
Does not replace team agreement during sprint planning.
GitHub commands require configured credentials and user-approved tool access.
Referenced helper scripts are not included in this package.

use_cases.title: Plan the next sprint
use_cases.description: Turn backlog notes, capacity data, and goals into a focused sprint plan.

use_cases.title: Review sprint health
use_cases.description: Assess progress, blockers, burndown risk, and scope options during an active sprint.

use_cases.title: Prepare team ceremonies
use_cases.description: Create clear inputs for planning, review, retrospective, and daily status discussions.

prompt_templates.title: Create a basic sprint plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner sprint planning from simple inputs.
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan our next two-week sprint. Use this backlog, our average velocity, team availability, and one sprint goal.

prompt_templates.title: Prioritize a backlog
prompt_templates.prompt: Prioritize these backlog items using RICE and MoSCoW. Explain the top sprint candidates and any dependencies.

prompt_templates.title: Assess mid-sprint risk
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced progress review during an active sprint.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this sprint status. Identify delivery risk, blockers, scope changes, and the best adjustment options.

prompt_templates.title: Build a capacity-based plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced planning with tradeoffs and constraints.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a sprint plan from this backlog, team calendar, velocity history, dependencies, and strategic goal. Include tradeoffs.

output_examples.input: Plan Sprint 12 for a two-week cycle with 28 historical points and five priority items.
output: A sprint goal tied to the highest priority outcome.
A capacity-based scope recommendation with buffer.
A short risk list with dependencies and mitigation steps.

output_examples.input: Prioritize ten backlog items before planning.
output: A ranked backlog using RICE and MoSCoW labels.
A clear split between must-have, should-have, and later work.
Notes about blockers, estimation gaps, and quick wins.

output_examples.input: Check whether our active sprint is on track.
output: A progress summary using completed work, remaining work, and elapsed time.
A risk assessment for blockers and scope creep.
Recommended actions for descoping, unblocking, or replanning.

best_practices: Provide current backlog, velocity, team availability, and known dependencies before asking for a plan.
Use the skill to support team discussion, then confirm scope with the delivery team.
Review sprint outcomes after each sprint so future capacity and risk estimates improve.
anti_patterns: Do not treat generated sprint scope as a team commitment without review.
Do not ignore dependencies, PTO, on-call work, or unplanned support load.
Do not use velocity to compare unrelated teams or pressure estimates.

faq.question: Can this skill create a sprint plan from a raw backlog?
faq.answer: Yes. It can structure backlog items into a sprint plan when priority, estimates, and capacity are available.

faq.question: Does it require GitHub access?
faq.answer: No. GitHub access is optional. You can paste backlog and sprint data directly into the prompt.

faq.question: Can it calculate team capacity?
faq.answer: Yes. It can estimate capacity from sprint length, team size, availability, holidays, and planned commitments.

faq.question: Can it help during an active sprint?
faq.answer: Yes. It can review progress, blockers, burndown risk, and scope adjustment options.

faq.question: Does it replace a scrum master or product owner?
faq.answer: No. It organizes planning information, but the team must agree on goals, estimates, and commitments.

faq.question: What data should I provide for best results?
faq.answer: Provide backlog items, estimates, priority signals, team availability, velocity history, deadlines, and dependencies.
